function_v0.name: templar

function_v0.doc:
Deposits `assets`, pulled from the vault, into the Templar vault with Templar's
own `convert_to_shares(assets)` as the minimum, and credits the vault with units for
the shares its balance rose by. The vault first collects its parts of settled
batches. `InvalidAmount` unless the strategy holds `assets` of USDC beyond what it
holds for vaults' paid claims; `ProtocolRejected` while
Templar's price stands above the gain bound, or if Templar refuses (paused, busy, its
value too old) or mints nothing. `change` is the position's value now minus the
value last recorded. The protocol total grows by `assets` (Q89), less what the
position's principal stood above its value (Q90).
function_v0.name: allocate

function_v0.doc: `vault`'s position, with its settled claims as if collected: units, value last\nreported, principal, what its claims still waiting on Templar count for, the USDC paid\nfor it and waiting, and how many claims still wait (at most two).
function_v0.name: position

function_v0.doc:
Pays `assets` to the vault, after it collects its parts of settled batches: first from
the USDC Templar paid for the vault's claims, then the rest by an atomic exit from the Templar vault's idle USDC, which may burn at
most the vault's own free shares. Units are burned for the shares the exit burned,
rounded up. The vault must receive exactly `assets`. Never gated by approval or the
protocol cap. `InsufficientPosition` if `assets` is above what the position can pay
now (its paid USDC plus its free shares at their counted value);
`InsufficientLiquidity` when the rest is above Templar's `max_withdraw` for the
strategy (its idle USDC; 0 while it is paused or busy); `ProtocolRejected` if Templar
refuses anyway or pays the vault anything but exactly `assets`. The
protocol total loses the principal taken out (Q89), and whatever of the rest stands
above the position's value (Q90).
function_v0.name: deallocate

function_v0.doc: Anyone: settles the batch in flight from what Templar sent back (see `settle`), then\nfiles the open batch if none is in flight and Templar takes it.
function_v0.name: sync_exits

function_v0.doc:
The vault's free shares and its shares in the open batch at their counted value
(Templar's `convert_to_assets`, rounded down, and no more than the gain-bounded price),
plus its claim on the batch in flight at that batch's counted payout (pro rata,
rounded down), plus the USDC paid for it; settled claims count as if collected. The
value last recorded when Templar does not answer. Never fails and never writes.
function_v0.name: real_assets

function_v0.doc: The cap on `total_allocated()`; 0 means none.
function_v0.name: protocol_cap

function_v0.doc:
A core vault's allocator or sentinel (`caller`, in that vault's own `config()`) queues
an exit of about `assets` of the vault's position at the Templar vault: the shares an
exit of `assets` takes leave the vault's free position and join the open batch, which
goes to Templar as one request, paid to the strategy itself, as soon as no batch is in
flight (this call files it when none is). Until then the shares keep earning; once
filed, the claim counts at the payout Templar fixed and earns nothing. Returns the
batch joined. `NotAuthorized` for any other caller; `InsufficientPosition` if the
shares are more than the vault's free shares; `InvalidAmount` if they are worth less
than Templar's minimum request; `ProtocolRejected` if Templar does not answer.
function_v0.name: request_exit
__constructor

function_v0.doc:
Anyone: lowers `vault`'s principal, and the protocol total by the same amount, to the
position's value now when that is lower, and emits `PrincipalSynced`. Never raises it,
moves no money and reports no `change`. A position that does not exist, or a Templar
vault that does not answer, is left as it is (Q90). `InvalidData` unless `data` names
the Templar vault.
function_v0.name: sync_position

function_v0.doc:
What `deallocate(vault, data, x)` can pay right now: the USDC paid for the vault's
claims plus what an atomic exit of its free shares can take from Templar's idle
(`max_withdraw` of the strategy, which counts every vault's shares, so it is taken
with the vault's own counted value). Settled claims count as if collected; claims
still waiting on Templar are not in it. 0 on malformed `data` or a failed read. Never
writes.
function_v0.name: max_deallocate

function_v0.doc: Sum of the principal every vault has put in and not taken out (Q89).

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Requests gathered into one Templar request. Stages: `STAGE_OPEN` (gathering, its shares
still in the strategy), `STAGE_FILED` (Templar's escrow; at most one batch at a time),
`STAGE_PAID` (Templar paid `expected`), `STAGE_REFUNDED` (Templar handed the shares back).
A settled batch is removed once every member has collected its part.
